title: A constant-factor step towards Vizing's conjecture
summary: Vizing's conjecture from 1963, considered by many the most important open problem in the field of graph domination, states that all graphs $G$ and $H$ satisfy $$γ(G\square H)\ge γ(G)γ(H),$$ where $γ$ denotes the domination number and $\square$ the Cartesian product. In a seminal result, Clark and Suen (2000) proved an approximate form of the conjecture, namely that $γ(G\square H)\ge \frac{1}{2}γ(G)γ(H)$ for all graphs $G$ and $H$.
